scope: Escape closes the frontmost open gameplay container before opening Options; development alpha
cause: The imported gameplay Escape handler opened Options unconditionally while UI keys were enabled.
implementation: Search open windows from back to front and select the frontmost ContainerWindow, independently of pointer position and game-window keyboard focus.
Reuse cmdCloseButtonFunc, including original object onClose scripts, open flags, mental-container deletion and deferred cleanup.
Consume that Escape after container closure; only open Options if no container is open.
Modal dialogs retain their own Escape handling, and O continues to open Options above an open container.
Update the in-game Hot Keys description; no external API, preference or CLI option added.

physical_container.name: Sack
physical_container.source: Existing unlocked physical container from the original save; the same ContainerWindow and callback used by chests.

checks: Open the physical object through its original open handler and verify its window and open flag.
O opens Options over the physical container; modal Escape returns to that still-open container.
Open Ideas, Skills and Memories in turn above the physical container. Escape with the pointer outside closes only the frontmost mental window.
A second Escape closes the physical container, clears its open flag, deletes its node and restores the game window.
Alternate between container focus and clicking the game background before physical closure.
After the last closure, Escape opens Options; another Escape returns to gameplay.
Actor identity and coordinates, party flags, UI settings and audio preferences remain unchanged.
The existing timed ambient audio may advance RNG during these nonmodal tests; original simulation behavior is preserved.
Prior keypad, save/load, Hot Keys, speech, music, document cursor and wheel regressions also pass.

memory.environment: Executed outside the sandbox to permit thread inspection

windows.build: Zig cross-build, Windows x64 Release, SDL 3.4.18
windows.execution: Native Windows processes from a preflight complete ZIP, using bundled-data discovery from an unrelated working directory

packages.validation: Final archives preserve the executable and SDL library tested in the preflight complete package; the eight-file allowlist is unchanged.

limitations: Automated injected SDL input, without a new manual keyboard or mouse hardware test
Physical regression uses an original-data Sack; chest windows share the same production handler
